description:
A Cloud-Native .NET Unit / Integration / Load / Hyper-CD testing tool that clusters automatically. Harness the power of your existing test suite to optimise the quality of your App. Install this as a tool or reference it to integrate closely with thebfg

      > dotnet tool install thebfg -g
releaseNotes:
2.2.2

      Changes:
        * Full CLI help reference printed for `bfg help`, `bfg ?`, `-h`/`--help` or no command (replaces the short usage blurb) - covers target/fire, deploy, profile, environment and its subcommands, arena, cmd, self and agent.
        * `bfg agent skills` / `bfg agent skill <name>` are now wired into dispatch and print the embedded skill (previously unreachable, fell through to the help text).

      2.2.1

      Fixes:
        * Local runs on Linux now work from a plain `dotnet tool install -g thebfg`. The self-hosted arena defaults to port 888 (privileged, < 1024), which a non-root user cannot bind - it now falls back to a free port automatically, and the in-process worker follows. No change where 888 already binds (root / cluster, macOS).

      theBFG is a framework-agnostic deploying and testing tool that clusters automatically. Point it at a test suite in any stack — .NET, Python, Node / TS / JS, JMeter — and it stands up a Test Arena plus a fleet of workers that shard the run, on your laptop or across a cloud fleet; point it at your system under test and it provisions and tears that down too. It is also an agentic AI tool: it gives your AI agent a set of these tools to call directly — discover and drive your suites, deploy and provision clusters, read back results — with built-in guardrails, and without the token overhead of a full MCP server. Full capability reference ships in docs/FEATURES.md.

      Cluster / environment types (thebfg environment up/down/estimate <name>):
        Worker-cluster adapters — docker, vmss (Azure VM Scale Sets), k8s, aks, macos-sim.
        App-host adapters (provision the system under test from your repo's config):
          * gke-host — Google Kubernetes Engine (Workload Identity, KEDA, Managed Kafka, GCS, Artifact Registry).
          * vmss-host, aks-host, bicep-host, aca-host, gcp-cloudrun-host, gcp-cloudrun-workers, docker-host.

      Also:
        * Guardrails — the arena checks cost, duration, idle, error-rate and p95 against every live environment ~once a minute and acts automatically (warn / stop / tear down).
        * Cost estimation — table-driven ratecard.json; `thebfg environment estimate` prints a per-resource breakdown and hourly total; the arena shows a live burn rate.
        * Perf monitor — a real-time arena dashboard plus a Cost & guardrails page.
        * Test catalogue — named suites (seed / verify / ui / perf) a person picks and runs from the arena.
        * Multi-language arenas — .NET (dotnet test / vstest), Python (pytest), Node / TS / JS (Karma / Jasmine / npm), clustered and sharded.
        * JMeter scale-set load testing; PerfView profiling (beta).

      Platform: .NET 10. Ships as a global dotnet tool:  dotnet tool install -g thebfg

      This project is under active development. Submit feature requests, Issues and feedback @ github
